Theorem
[Comparison and uniqueness] Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0045 1. ch3:3.3\group ch03-classical-maximum-principle Let $c\leq 0$, and let $u,v\in C^2(\Omega )\cap C^0(\overline\Omega )$. If $Lu\geq Lv$ in $\Omega $ and $u\leq v$ on $\partial \Omega $, then $u\leq v$ in $\Omega $. In particular, equal equations and equal boundary values imply $u=v$.
Proof

\sketch Apply Corollary 6 to $u-v$.

□
